payload.selection_rationale:
One proposal (practice), taken as the core, checked against what the survey and spikes measured. It fits the code as it is. RuleCases.ps1 already has a script-scope `$Twinned`, SL-053's `Get-ExpectedSettled` (209-233) and `New-ParityRoot`, which copies the tree's own yaml and .cs. Deriving `$Twinned` and feeding it to the existing settled derivation is the smallest change that fixes the bug. The reported bug is only a title, so I assumed the acceptance is the repro `tests/bugs/SL-069-RuleCasesDeriveCounts.Tests.ps1` exiting 0. On top of that, C-001..C-005 must stay green on the clean tree under powershell.exe and pwsh, and both `SettledCountProbe -Shape Misclassified` and `-Shape GuardRule` must still exit 0.

The proposal departs on purpose from the slice text ('read the numbers from the parity output'). I kept the departure because a measurement backs it. The build check ran `SettledCountProbe -Shape Misclassified` and it passes today only because C-001's expected counts are independent of the tool. Reading them back makes C-001 agree with any count the tool prints. The spike `parity-counts-recountable-independently` (go) reproduced 11/15/27/47 with about 20 lines of regex that never touch eng/rules-parity.ps1, identically on 5.1 and 7. The spike `agree-sites-move-in-lockstep-with-baseline` (conditional) supplies the per-site offsets. Both are encoded as constraints below.

Four things are mine, not the proposal's:
1. A sibling scratch-tree test. The committed repro exercises only C-001, but six other sites went stale in SL-039/042/043.
2. The guard regexes are tightened to match what is wrong: five regexes on one file, with `\bTwinned\s*=\s*\d` replacing `\$Twinned\s*=\s*\d`.
3. The recount stays inside RuleCases.ps1, because the repro and the spike copy selected files into a scratch tree and a new sibling file might not be copied.
4. SettledCountProbe.ps1:125 is recorded as a known residual, not silently ignored.

C-003's lookahead is already in HEAD and is untouched. The settled half was built by SL-053 and is reused.

Nothing new was decided at stack level. The suite stays PowerShell 5.1/7, the language already in use for rules-parity, so `stack_chosen` is empty.

components.name: Get-RuleCounts (independent recount)
components.responsibility: Reads $Repo's own tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/ArchitectureRulesTests.cs and .taad/fitness.yaml and returns Facts, Twinned and Patterns. Facts = lines matching '^\s*\[\s*(Fact|Theory)\b'. Patterns = lines matching '^\s*@".*"\s*(,|\);)\s*$'. Twinned = '^  - name:' lines above the FIRST '^\s*#\s*settled by SL-' line. Lines are read with [IO.File]::ReadAllLines so BOM and encoding behave the same on 5.1 and 7. It never calls, dot-sources or parses the output of eng/rules-parity.ps1. It throws, and the script exits non-zero before any case runs, when a file is missing, no settled marker is found, or any count is 0. There is no fallback to a literal.
components.key_interactions: Called once from the main block after the function definitions, with $Repo. Result kept in $script:Counts, then `$Twinned = $script:Counts.Twinned` replaces the literal at line 35. Get-ExpectedSettled (209-233) is unchanged and now subtracts the derived value. The recount stays in RuleCases.ps1 (no new file) so scratch copies that carry only the selected files still work.

components.name: Format-AgreeLine
components.responsibility: The only place that spells 'rules-parity: AGREE {Facts} facts <- {Twinned} twinned entries, {Patterns} patterns; {Settled} settled entries not compared'. The existing prefix or substring matching stays as it is. Only the construction of the expected string changes.
components.key_interactions: Coupled to the wording of eng/rules-parity.ps1's AGREE line. Called by C-001, C-003, C-004, C-005, C-008. Settled always comes from Get-ExpectedSettled.

components.name: Case sites rewired with measured offsets
components.responsibility: Every literal becomes arithmetic on the clean-tree recount, with a one-line comment naming the mutation behind each offset. C-001 (238/240/243): offsets 0,0,0,0 and -ExpectFacts = $Counts.Facts. C-003 (305): N/M/P +0, settled through Get-ExpectedSettled (+1 relative to clean). C-004 (326, four BOM spellings): 0. C-005 (369-370): -ExpectFacts = Facts+1, message 'found $Facts ... has $($Facts+1)'. C-005 fixture (408): 0. C-007 (600): 'xunit $($Counts.Facts) Facts'. C-008 (625): Twinned-1, because the tests-scope twin of InteropLivesOnlyInNative is deleted. C-008 (633): 0. C-009's bare 'AGREE' is left alone. Expectations are always clean-recount + offset, never a recount of a mutated fixture.
components.key_interactions: Fixtures come from New-ParityRoot, which copies $Repo's own files. That is why constant offsets hold (lockstep spike, 11 tree states).

components.name: Count-free case titles
components.responsibility: Titles such as 'the clean tree: 11 Facts, 15 twinned entries, 27 patterns, ...' drop their numbers. Nothing parses titles, so there is no ordering dependency and they cannot go stale.

components.name: Literal-parity-count guard (fitness rule)
components.responsibility: One settled (non-twinned, no [Fact]) entry under a new '  # settled by SL-069' marker after the existing settled block, in the shape of SL-053's rule at .taad/fitness.yaml:602. Scoped to tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1. It forbids the literal-count regexes listed in architecture_rules. It must hit HEAD's RuleCases.ps1 and nothing in the fixed file.
components.key_interactions: Moves the real tree's settled count from 47 to 48. That is harmless because S is derived everywhere in RuleCases.ps1. It sits below the first marker, so the twinned count, the C-003 lookahead and the C-008 lookahead are unaffected. If the engine also writes architecture_rules into the registry, build must not add a second copy.

components.name: Committed repro
components.responsibility: Commit the untracked tests/bugs/SL-069-RuleCasesDeriveCounts.Tests.ps1 unchanged. It adds one Fact and one twinned entry to a scratch copy and requires C-001 to exit 0 under powershell.exe and pwsh.

components.name: Every-case-follows-counts sibling test
components.responsibility: Builds the same kind of scratch tree the repro does, in two variants (one single-scope Fact plus one twinned entry; one two-scope Fact plus two twinned entries). Runs the scratch copy's RuleCases.ps1 -Case C-001, C-003, C-004 and C-005 under pwsh and powershell.exe, and requires exit 0 and 'All checks held.' for each. C-007 and C-008 run in it only when -EnginePython/-EngineRoot are supplied.
components.key_interactions: Copies the same files the repro copies. The repro exercises only C-001, and the six other stale sites are what SL-039/042/043 actually left red.

contracts.name: Get-RuleCounts -Repo <path> -> [pscustomobject]@{Facts;Twinned;Patterns}
contracts.error_cases: Throws with a message naming the file and the missing thing ('no # settled by SL- marker in .taad/fitness.yaml', 'no [Fact] in ArchitectureRulesTests.cs', 'no @"..." pattern lines'). The script exits non-zero before any case runs and never substitutes 0 or a literal.
contracts.notes: Must stay independent of eng/rules-parity.ps1: no dot-sourcing, no invocation, no reading its output. If it did, SettledCountProbe -Shape Misclassified would go red because C-001 would stop failing on a miscounting tool.

contracts.name: Format-AgreeLine -Facts -Twinned -Patterns -Settled -> string
contracts.notes: Single spelling of the parity summary line. It must change together with the AGREE wording in eng/rules-parity.ps1.

contracts.name: RuleCases.ps1 -Case C-0NN [-EnginePython -EngineRoot]
contracts.error_cases: Parameters, 'ok'/'FAIL' rows, 'All checks held.', 'N check(s) failed.' and exit codes are unchanged. There is one new failure path: the recount throws and the script exits non-zero with the reason.
contracts.notes: Titles become count-free. The repro checks only the exit code and 'All checks held.'.

contracts.name: tests/bugs/SL-069-RuleCasesDeriveCounts.Tests.ps1
contracts.notes: Acceptance criterion. Exit 0 under pwsh, and the script itself drives powershell.exe and pwsh. On its scratch tree parity says 12/16/28 and C-001 must print 'All checks held.'.

contracts.name: tests/bugs/SL-069-EveryCaseFollowsCounts.Tests.ps1
contracts.notes: Exit 0 when C-001, C-003, C-004 and C-005 all hold on both scratch-tree variants under both hosts.

key_decisions.decision: Derive Facts, Twinned and Patterns from an independent recount of $Repo's yaml and .cs, not from eng/rules-parity.ps1's output. This departs from the slice text 'read the numbers from the parity output'.
key_decisions.rationale: Read-back makes C-001 agree with whatever the tool prints. SL-053's SettledCountProbe -Shape Misclassified requires C-001 to fail when the tool moves one twinned entry to settled, and it passes today. The recountable spike (go) matched parity exactly on the real tree, identically on 5.1 and 7, without using parity's parser. The slice's goal (no stale literals, green on the next twinned slice) is met either way, and only the recount keeps the oracle. The repro exiting 0 is satisfied by both.

key_decisions.decision: Recount the clean $Repo once and apply explicit per-site offsets. Do not recount each mutated fixture.
key_decisions.rationale: The lockstep spike measured the offsets constant over 11 tree states (C-003 settled +1, C-008 tests-scope-deleted twinned -1, all others 0). Recounting a mutated fixture was never measured and would let an expectation follow the very mutation the case exists to detect. The spike's constraints hold only while every AGREE fixture is built by New-ParityRoot from the tree's own files, which is true today.

key_decisions.decision: Keep Get-ExpectedSettled and every settled-side call as SL-053 left them. Only $Twinned becomes derived (assigned in the main block after the function definitions).
key_decisions.rationale: The spike's settled constraint is 'yaml item count minus the tree's own twinned count, not minus the constant 15'. That is exactly what feeding the derived value gives. It avoids a second settled derivation and leaves SL-053's guard probe untouched.

key_decisions.decision: The recount's Fact regex is looser than the parity reader's ('^\s*\[\s*(Fact|Theory)\b' rather than the spike's '^\s*\[(Fact|Theory)\]\s*$'). Build must run it on the clean tree first and require 11.
key_decisions.rationale: -ExpectFacts exists to catch a Fact the reader cannot see. A recount in the reader's own strict shape would make that check circular, and `[Fact(Skip=...)]` or `[Fact, Trait(...)]` would slip past both. If the looser regex yields more than 11 on the clean tree, that is a real reader gap to report, not a reason to narrow the regex. The loose form was not measured by any spike.

key_decisions.decision: C-005's deliberate mismatch is written as ExpectFacts = Facts+1, with the message 'found N ... has N+1'.
key_decisions.rationale: Spike constraint: a literal 12 turns into AGREE the moment the tree has 12 Facts, which silently disables the case.

key_decisions.decision: An unreadable or degenerate recount (missing file, no marker, zero count) fails the whole script before any case runs. It never falls back.
key_decisions.rationale: Spike constraint: a broken baseline must fail the script, not seed expectations. A 0 or a marker-less recount would otherwise become a plausible expected line.

key_decisions.decision: Add one settled fitness rule (under '# settled by SL-069') forbidding literal parity counts in RuleCases.ps1. Read-back is not given a regex rule; the Misclassified probe is its guard.
key_decisions.rationale: The repro protects only C-001; a textual guard covers every site, the same pattern SL-053 used for the settled half. Read-back can be spelled too many ways for a regex to catch, so a rule for it would be false comfort. The behavioural probe already catches it.

key_decisions.decision: Add a sibling scratch-tree test (single-scope and two-scope variants) that runs C-001, C-003, C-004 and C-005, and C-007/C-008 when the engine is supplied.
key_decisions.rationale: The lockstep spike measured parity lines, not the real cases, and the committed repro runs only C-001. Two-scope Facts (M+2, not M+1) are how SL-043 moved the counts.

key_decisions.decision: Keep the recount inside RuleCases.ps1 rather than a shared tests/rules/RuleCounts.ps1.
key_decisions.rationale: The repro and the spike copy selected files into a scratch tree, so a new sibling file might not be present there, and the repro cannot be changed. This has not been verified against the repro's copy list. A shared module would also tempt eng/rules-parity.ps1 to reuse the same counting code, which would tie the oracle to the tool.

key_decisions.decision: Leave tests/rules/SettledCountProbe.ps1:125 (a literal AGREE line for its stub tool) out of this slice.
key_decisions.rationale: It is outside the slice's named file. After the next twinned slice the Misclassified shape will still fail C-001, but it can no longer tell the misclassification apart from a stale stub line. That weakens the probe without inverting it: a read-back regression would still turn it red.

architecture_rules.name: the rule-case suite never pins a literal parity count
architecture_rules.because: A literal Facts/Twinned/Patterns count goes stale on the next slice that declares a twinned rule. That happened after SL-039, SL-042 and SL-043, and it turns every rule-copy case red or CANNOT-READ. The counts must come from the recount, and only an offset from it may be written. A literal in the C-005 mismatch case is worse: it silently turns into AGREE once the tree reaches that number.

cases.behaviour: run C-001 against a tree that declares one more twinned rule
cases.shape: the tree has one more single-scope Fact plus its twinned entry than the last baseline (12 facts, 16 twinned, 28 patterns)
cases.why: This is the reported bug. With literals, C-001 fails the pinned 11/15/27 string and `-ExpectFacts 11` returns CANNOT-READ (exit 2).

cases.behaviour: run C-001, C-003, C-004 and C-005 against a tree that declares a two-scope rule
cases.shape: the new Fact's twin is two yaml entries (arch scope and tests scope), so Twinned moves by 2 while Facts moves by 1
cases.why: Facts and twinned entries are different counts (11 facts vs 15 entries). A recount that maps one Fact to one entry, or an offset assuming +1, breaks only on this shape. SL-043 moved the counts this way. The committed repro covers only the single-scope shape.

cases.shape: the tree has N Facts and again N+1 Facts; the case passes N+1
cases.why: A literal 12 flips to AGREE when the tree reaches 12 Facts and the case stops testing anything. The expected exit stays 2 (CANNOT-READ) and the message must say 'found N ... has N+1'.

cases.behaviour: C-003 the twin of a one-scope Fact deleted
cases.shape: the added twinned entry is the last one above the settled marker, and the case's expected settled count is one higher than clean
cases.why: The narrowed lookahead `(?=^  - name:|^  # settled by SL-)` ends the block at the marker. Settled must be derived as yaml items minus the derived twinned count, not minus 15, or D1/D2/D4-style trees give a wrong expectation.

cases.shape: the InteropLivesOnlyInNative tests-scope twin appears once in the yaml, and the expected line is Twinned-1 with Facts and Patterns unchanged
cases.why: The M-1 offset assumes that entry is unique. The survey and spikes never ran the real C-008 or C-007 (no engine), only the mutated parity line, so this is unverified until run with the engine.

cases.behaviour: Get-RuleCounts on a yaml with more than one settled marker
cases.shape: the real tree after this slice: the existing '# settled by SL-' markers plus the new SL-069 one below them, so the clean line is 11/15/27/48
cases.why: Twinned is defined as the entries above the FIRST marker. A recount that stops at the last marker, or resets at each, miscounts. C-001 must be green on the real tree after the new settled entry lands.

cases.shape: no '# settled by SL-' marker in the yaml
cases.why: Without a marker the twinned/settled split is undefined. It must exit non-zero before any case with a message naming the marker, not seed expectations.

cases.shape: ArchitectureRulesTests.cs is missing, or has zero [Fact] or zero pattern lines
cases.why: A count of 0 would otherwise become a plausible expected line ('AGREE 0 facts') and a wrong pass or a confusing fail. No fallback to a literal is allowed.

cases.behaviour: C-001 catches a miscounting parity tool (SettledCountProbe -Shape Misclassified)
cases.shape: the tool moves one twinned entry to settled (14 twinned, one more settled)
cases.why: This is the reason for the independent recount. Read-back would make C-001 pass and the probe go red. Must still exit 0 after the change, on the real tree.

cases.behaviour: C-001 with a Fact the parity reader cannot see
cases.shape: a Fact spelled `[Fact(Skip=...)]` or `[Fact, Trait(...)]`, which the loose recount regex counts
cases.why: That is the point of the looser regex. C-001 must go red (the tool AGREEs on fewer Facts, or CANNOT-READs), and must not agree with the tool by sharing its blind spot.

cases.shape: the same tree run under both hosts, including the recount's regexes and file reading
cases.why: The recount must return identical counts on both (measured identical by the spike). The repro and the sibling test run both hosts.

cases.behaviour: literal-count guard rule (SettledCountProbe -Shape GuardRule plus Select-String)
cases.shape: HEAD's RuleCases.ps1 (literals at lines 35, 238/240, 243, 305, 326, 370, 408, 600, 625, 633) versus the fixed file
cases.why: A guard that matches nothing, or fires on correct code (the `AGREE $($x) facts` template, the count-free titles), is worthless. It must hit the pre-fix file and stay silent on the fixed one, and SL-053's own guard must stay silent too.

cases.behaviour: Get-RuleCounts reading a file with a BOM
cases.shape: the tree's own yaml or .cs starts with a UTF-8 BOM
cases.why: A BOM affects only line 1, which is never a [Fact], a pattern line or a '  - name:' line. ReadAllLines strips it. C-004 already covers parity's own BOM reading.

cases.behaviour: C-007 'xunit N Facts' against the trx
cases.shape: the test class contains a [Theory] with several data rows, so trx results exceed source attributes
cases.why: There is no [Theory] in ArchitectureRulesTests.cs today. If one is added, C-007 fails loudly on the count mismatch rather than passing silently, so a test is not owed now.

proposals.note: The only proposal. Taken whole: independent recount, measured offsets, derived $Twinned into Get-ExpectedSettled, count-free titles, literal-count guard, committed repro. Additions: the sibling scratch-tree test, tightened guard regexes, an explicit note that the recount stays in RuleCases.ps1, and the SettledCountProbe.ps1:125 residual recorded. Nothing else was dropped.

payload.coherence_check:
One proposal, so there is no composition across proposals to check, and nothing here has yet survived a disagreement. Its first lines of attack are: (1) the deliberate departure from the slice text 'read the numbers from the parity output', (2) the looser Fact regex, which no spike measured, and (3) the constant per-site offsets.

I checked the pieces inside the single proposal for contradictory invariants:
- Independence vs derivation. The recount (independent of the tool) feeds both the N/M/P expectations and, through $Twinned, Get-ExpectedSettled. Everything therefore comes from one source, with one error contract: an unreadable input throws before any case runs. There is no second path that reads the tool's output, so no expectation can be tool-derived by accident. What I changed at that seam: Get-RuleCounts is located inside RuleCases.ps1 (not a shared file) so that it cannot become the tool's counting code.
- The new settled fitness entry moves the clean tree from 47 to 48 settled. That contradicts nothing, because S is derived everywhere and the rule sits below the first marker. The Twinned definition (above the FIRST marker) is what keeps the positional count stable when a later marker is added. The scratch trees copy the tree's own yaml, so they inherit the new entry and move in lockstep.
- Offsets vs derivation. The offsets are relative to the clean recount and were measured on parity lines, not on real cases. That is why the sibling test exists.

What no stage settled:
- C-006..C-014 need the TAAD engine and were run by neither the build check nor the spikes. The C-007 and C-008 rewrites rest on parity lines measured from the same mutations, not on the real cases running. Build must run them with -EnginePython/-EngineRoot, or record that they were not run.
- Whether the repro copies selected files or a whole directory is unverified, and the recount's location depends on it.
- The recount was measured only at the clean tree (11/15/27/47). It is unmeasured on the repro's scratch tree until the repro is run.
- The recount is tied to the .cs coding style (verbatim `@"..."` pattern lines). If the next Fact spells its pattern differently, C-001 goes red with both lines shown. That is loud, but it is a cost of not reading back.

cross_domain_transfer.source_domain: Batch data-processing audit: control totals (hash totals) in reconciliation
cross_domain_transfer.pattern: The expected total is computed from the source documents by a route separate from the system being checked, then compared to the total that system reports. It is never taken from the system's own report, because then reconciliation proves nothing. Here the source documents are fitness.yaml and ArchitectureRulesTests.cs, the checked system is eng/rules-parity.ps1, and the control total is Get-RuleCounts.
cross_domain_transfer.rationale: It is the exact tension the build check found. The slice text asks for read-back, SL-053's Misclassified probe requires an independent control, and the recountable spike showed an independent control costs about 20 lines of regex. It restates SL-053's own stance rather than introducing a new one, so it is low risk.

invariants.precondition: The control count is computed without the checked system's code or output
invariants.evidence: parity-counts-recountable-independently: recount.ps1 never reads or calls rules-parity.ps1.

invariants.precondition: The recount's definitions reproduce the tool's numbers on the clean tree
invariants.evidence: Recount 11/15/27/47 equals parity's line exactly, identical on pwsh 7.6.6 and powershell.exe 5.1.

invariants.precondition: Per-site deltas from the clean tree are constant across tree states
invariants.evidence: agree-sites-move-in-lockstep-with-baseline: offsets constant over 11 trees for C-001/003/004/005/008, conditional on the fixtures being built by New-ParityRoot.

invariants.precondition: The recount moves with a twinned-rule addition (12/16/28 on the repro's scratch tree, and two-scope variants)
invariants.evidence: Not measured directly. The repro and the sibling test exiting 0 are the check.

invariants.precondition: A miscounting tool still fails C-001
invariants.evidence: SettledCountProbe -Shape Misclassified exits 0 today. It must still exit 0 after the change.

invariants.precondition: The loose Fact regex yields 11 on the clean tree
invariants.evidence: Only the strict regex was measured (11). The loose one was not run.

invariants.precondition: In a scratch copy, $Repo resolves to the scratch root, and the scratch copy contains everything the recount reads
invariants.evidence: The spike's driver ran the cases against scratch trees, which suggests it does. Nothing measured the repro's own copy list.

decidable_disagreements.question: Should RuleCases.ps1's expected Facts/Twinned/Patterns come from an independent recount of the yaml and .cs, or from the parity tool's own output as the slice text says?
decidable_disagreements.positions: Slice text: read them from the parity output (no recount code to maintain, immune to .cs style). Practice proposal: recount independently, because SL-053's Misclassified probe passes today only while C-001's expectations are independent of the tool, and read-back would turn that probe red. Reality settles it: run SettledCountProbe -Shape Misclassified under each, and check that the recount equals parity on the clean tree, the repro's scratch tree and the two-scope tree.

taste_disagreements: Count-free case titles versus titles computed from the recount (the proposal chose count-free; computed titles need the counts to exist before the cases are declared).
A separate Format-AgreeLine function versus inline string interpolation at each site (one spelling chosen, at the price of a function to keep in step with the parity tool's wording).

The recount in RuleCases.ps1 versus a shared tests/rules/RuleCounts.ps1 that SettledCountProbe.ps1 could also use. The in-file placement was chosen because of the scratch-copy risk, but a shared file would make the SettledCountProbe.ps1:125 follow-up cheaper.
One literal-count guard rule with five regexes versus a second rule against reading counts back (rejected: read-back has too many spellings for a regex to catch).
open_questions: Should tests/rules/SettledCountProbe.ps1:125 (the stub tool's literal AGREE line) be derived from the recount in this slice, or left as a follow-up? It is outside the slice's named file. Left as-is, the Misclassified probe still turns red on a read-back regression, but after the next twinned slice it can no longer tell a real misclassification from a stale stub line.

prior_art.pattern: Parity fixtures are emitted by a separate reference implementation, and only the invariants that survive version skew are pinned. Expectations come from a different implementation than the one under test.

Layered case assertions include a count-consistency check: the number of golden statements must equal an independently declared roundTrips count, and results must match an independent reference query.

Snapshot and approval tests that regenerate expectations from the system under test (Jest -u, ApprovalTests 'approve all') rubber-stamp regressions. This is the known failure mode of 'read the expected value back from the tool'.
Test-oracle problem and pseudo-oracles: an independently written computation serves as the oracle for a program whose output cannot be hand-checked.
Batch control and hash totals are computed at the source and reconciled against the processing system's reported totals.
